title: Hired 3 marketing agencies in 2 years — all terrible. What am I doing wrong?

variant_a.content:
I watched a law firm owner's face sink when she realized the truth.

Three years of "marketing partnerships." $57K spent. 12 cases signed.

Then she asked the question that changed everything: "What are we actually measuring?"

Agency 1: Promised 20 leads/month. Delivered 3. No call tracking. No reporting.

Agency 2: Beautiful reports. Clicks up, CTR up, cases down. Optimizing vanity metrics.

Agency 3: Ran ads to the wrong zip code for 4 months. Billed $2K/month the whole time.

The real problem: none measured what matters.

Signed cases. That's it.

Before you hire anyone, ask three things:

1. "How do you define a lead?" (If they say clicks, run.)
2. "What's my cost per signed case?" (If they don't know, run.)
3. "Can I access all accounts?" (If no, run.)

Good agencies welcome accountability.

Bad ones hide behind impressions.

variant_b.content:
$57K. 12 cases. $4,750 per case.

Those are the real numbers from a law firm that hired three "top" agencies.

Here's the breakdown of what actually happened.

Agency 2: Beautiful reports. Clicks up, CTR up, cases down. Optimizing vanity metrics.

hypothesis: Variant B (data-driven) should perform better. Law firm owners and B2B service providers on LinkedIn respond strongly to concrete numbers upfront—they immediately see ROI relevance. Variant A creates curiosity through narrative, which may engage some audiences but risks lower click-through rates. For legal services professionals, specificity signals credibility and relevance faster than storytelling alone.
